bull.b: Expansion from handheld systems to Environment Systems across two facilities, alongside a recurring BIT Solution agreement, shows SteraMist can deepen within regulated customers. This supports repeat consumable revenue and a broader installed-base opportunity beyond one-time equipment sales.

Q2 revenue rose 118% year over year and the backlog reached $2.6 million post-quarter, while booked orders and expected completions exceeded $6.2 million. These indicators improve near-term revenue visibility and demonstrate growing commercial traction if execution continues.

An unconditional EPA registration for AgriMist, additional EU/UK approvals, and new utility-patent filings broaden the platform’s addressable applications and protection. Wider regulatory coverage can support adoption across food safety and international markets over the coming quarters.

bear.b: Operating cash flow has been negative in every period shown, with TTM cash flow around -$1.30B and negative free cash flow. Persistent cash consumption limits self-funded growth and leaves the company more dependent on external capital to sustain operations.

Debt-to-equity rose to about 2.17x TTM and 5.82x in 2025, alongside steep losses and negative ROE. This deterioration reduces financial flexibility, increases refinancing pressure, and can constrain investment in scaling the SteraMist platform.

Key growth opportunities, including FDA 510(k) clearance, an FDA FCN, and further international registrations, remain contingent on studies and approvals. Delays or unfavorable outcomes could postpone commercialization and weaken the conversion of the pipeline into revenue.
